headline: A paper shows policy shifts can invalidate one-step world-model coverage, then tests ratio-weighted recalibration
summary: The Aug 20, 2026 preprint studies uncertainty calibration when a fixed robot world model is evaluated under a changed action-selection policy. Under a shared conditional transition mechanism, it derives a density-ratio correction for transporting one-step marginal conformal coverage and a bound linking estimated-ratio error to coverage loss. In an author-run experiment using 192 physical Franka transitions from 15 episodes, the predictor remains fixed while the evaluation pool is reweighted by an outcome-blind action-magnitude statistic. At nominal 90% coverage and the strongest controlled shift, ordinary source calibration covers 55.0%; oracle and learned ratio weighting cover 91.0% and 90.9%. The study is paper-reported and does not test a new live policy rollout: the target distribution is a controlled reweighting of the same finite pool. Its guarantees require shared conditional dynamics and are one-step and marginal, not joint trajectory guarantees.
